_readme: DRAFT. CQ texts and the scheme list come from the SPR (ea361093-SPR.md), unverified against the book. Every locus is a draft, needs review.

cqs.text: What evidence supports the claim that A is generally accepted as true?
cqs.note: the intended assumption generally_accepted(A) is under the misspelled key 'assumption:' and is dropped at load; generally_true/1 and generally_accepted/1 say the same thing

cqs.text: Even if A is generally accepted, are there good reasons to doubt that it is true?
What actions or other indications show that a large majority accepts A?
Even if a large majority accepts A, what grounds are there for thinking they are justified?
Does the context of dialogue require a particular level of precision?
cqs.note: F is not a declared variable of the scheme (declares P instead)

cqs.text: Is the property F too vague to meet that level of precision?
Why is this vagueness a problem in the dialogue in which the argument was advanced?
cqs.note: maps to the warrant premise; could instead be an argument-locus question

cqs.text: Does the context of dialogue require a nonarbitrary definition?
cqs.note: written needed_nonarbitrary((A,F) in walton.yml: unparsable, silently dropped until fixed

cqs.text: Is the property F defined arbitrarily?
Why is the arbitrariness a problem in this dialogue?
Are there alternative means of realizing the goal?

cqs.note: CQ1 and CQ2 share one exception; consider alternative_means(G,A) for CQ1 (predicate exists in the collection)

cqs.text: What is the strength of the correlation between the sign and the event signified?

cqs.text: How satisfactory is the explanation itself, apart from the alternatives available so far?

cqs.text: How far has the dialogue progressed (how thorough was the investigation)?

cqs.text: Is it the case that if A (the hypothesis) is true then B is true?
Has B been observed (to be true)?
Could there be some reason why B is true other than the hypothesis?

Has B been observed to be false?
Could there be another reason for the observation?
